newsitem.title: USA: Florida Progress Crystal River costs up.
newsitem.headline: Florida Progress Crystal River costs up.

text.p: Florida Power Corp said Monday 1997 operation and maintenance costs for its Crystal River 3 nuclear power plant are now projected to be substantially higher than previously reported.

The Florida Progress Corp subsidiary said it estimates these "expenditures could range from $80 million to $100 million higher than its original target for 1997 nuclear O & M costs. Total O & M expenditures for the nuclear plant could range from $170 million to $190 million in 1997.
"Additional capital costs for 1997 could range from $30 million to $45 million," the company continued.
This would increase total capital expenditures for Crystal River 3 to $40 million to $55 million, the utility said.
Previously, Florida Power had been projecting total 1997 capital spending of $372.1 million, up from 1996 spending of $217.3 million.
It had projected spending would decline each year through 2000 -- to $306.6 million next year, $252.3 million in 1999 and $230.1 million in 2000.
The company said it does not plan to seek recovery of these additional outage costs through a rate increase.

The 860 megawatt power plant, Florida Power's only nuclear unit, was taken off-line on September 2, 1996, to repair a cracked lube-oil pipe. After repairs were made on the pipe, the company continued the shutdown to perform modifications on the plant's emergency cooling system. Similar changes have been necessary at other U.S. nuclear plants of the same design, it pointed out.
Florida Power said Crystal River 3 is expected to return to service by the end of this year.
The utility said it met last week with officials from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in Atlanta to discuss progress relating to the restart of the nuclear plant.

Last week's meetings included an update to the NRC relating to the plant's "System Readiness Review Program." To date, the company said, this effort has involved over 8,000 system checks and over 10,000 worker hours. So far, none of the discrepancies has impacted the company's planned restart date, it said.
The company will complete its review by the end of July.
At a Restart Panel meeting, the company said, it informed the NRC that design basis modification work was progressing as planned.

Florida Power said the expected year-end restart date is based on completion of upgrades to the emergency feedwater system and emergency diesel generators. Work related to these modifications is expected to be completed by November, allowing time for NRC license amendments and final regulatory approval.
It said operations and maintenance costs associated with the modifications have not significantly changed.

"However, the additional work necessary to complete the 'System Readiness Review Program' and resolution of associated issues resulted in the 1997 cost projection being "substantially higher than previously reported," it said.
